In summary, our research is concerned with
the analysis of the molecular mechanisms involved in the metastasis of breast cancer.
the analysis of the expression of the epidermoid growth factor receptor (c-erbB-1) and its closely related oncogene c-erbB-2 (HER 2/neu) in human breast cancer.
the identification of factors involved in the metastatic process of mammary carcinoma.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the erbB 2 oncoproteins are important for the invasion and motility in breast cancer.
erbB 1 and erbB 1 are both expressed in breast cancer cells, but only erbB 2 seems to be associated with the invasive and metastatic phenotype of these cells.
erbB 3 and erbB 4 are not involved in breast cancer invasion, while the erbB 2 expression is correlated with invasivity and metastasis of mammary carcinoma cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the expression of erbB 1 and erbB 3 receptors does not correlate with the invasive potential of breast cancer cells.
metastatic cells and cell clusters are selected during tumor progression and that these cells are characterized by expression of the erbB onco genes.
metastasis in breast carcinoma is a multi-step process, which is controlled by the expression of erbB 1 and erbB 3 oncogenes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the expression of erbB 1, erbB 2, and erbB 3 in the primary tumor does not correlate with the expression of the receptors in the metastatic lesions.
